assertion: A typical Thanksgiving dinner in 2026 will cost about $80, or $8 per person, according to agricultural industry researchers.
why_not: The ERS passage with '$8' is an unrelated dollar figure ($836.8 billion); it says nothing about Thanksgiving dinner cost.
why_no_page: AFBF's 2026 survey page loaded but carries no results yet (release Nov. 18); no other page with a 2026 total was found.
reason: AFBF 2026 survey results are not published until Nov. 18; 2025 expanded menu was $77.09 ($7.71 per person), so $80 is plausible but unconfirmed.
searched: Farm Bureau Thanksgiving dinner survey 2026 cost 10 people $8 per person

assertion: Expert explains why farmers earn less than you would think from Thanksgiving feasts
source_finding: ERS farm share is gross returns to farms (18.5c/7.1c), not farmer earnings; net farm value added is lower still (6.7c per food dollar overall).
inaccuracy: Headline says 'earn' but figures are gross receipts shares of retail spending, not income.
independent_value: ERS: gross farm share 11.8c overall; value added 6.7c

assertion: For meals at home, based on 2024 data, farmers will get about $0.19 on the retail dollar or 19%.
speaker: George Davis

assertion: So, for a Thanksgiving meal made at home of $80, the farmer gets about $15. The remaining $65 goes toward those other marketing inputs.
speaker: George Davis
inaccuracy: Arithmetic right (19% of 80 = 15.2) but applies the all-groceries average to a holiday basket.

assertion: Nowadays, households spend about 56% of their food dollars on dining out.
speaker: George Davis
inaccuracy: ERS puts food away from home at 58.9% of food spending in 2024; 56.3% is an inflation-adjusted 2025 figure.
searched: ERS share of food expenditures food away from home 2024

assertion: If a Thanksgiving take-out meal costs $750 for a family of 10, or $75 per person, farmers only get about $.07 on the dollar, or 7%, so the farmer would get about $53 from that $750.
speaker: George Davis
inaccuracy: 7.1 cents is the average for all food away from home, applied to a take-out meal; arithmetic correct (52.5).

assertion: For a $180 'heat and serve' meal from Cracker Barrel, the farmer gets only about $13.
speaker: George Davis
inaccuracy: 7.1% of $180 is $12.78, correct; the 7% average is assumed for this product and third-party prices run about $175-190.
searched: Cracker Barrel Thanksgiving Heat n' Serve 2026 price serves

assertion: In a very real sense, when we buy ingredients for a meal, or an actual meal, we are mainly buying convenience or marketing services, not food.
speaker: George Davis
source_finding: ERS marketing share is 81.5c (home) and 92.9c (away) but covers processing, transport, retailing and labor, not just convenience.
inaccuracy: Marketing share figures are right but they pay for essential transformation and distribution, not only convenience.
